outcome: presence of subserosal hypoechoic rim sign on ultrasound
presence of endomyometrial junction indistinctness on ultrasound
cohort: 62 postpartum patients presenting to Auckland City Hospital: 31 with acute endometritis and 31 randomly selected controls with other postpartum complications.
finding: Identifying the subserosal hypoechoic rim and endomyometrial junction indistinctness on ultrasound scans can reliably help to distinguish patients with acute postpartum endometritis from other postpartum complications, particularly in full-term postpartum patients.
